name: Parc
description: This bustling Parisian-style brasserie anchors the east side of Rittenhouse Square and stays packed from morning coffee through late-night dinner. Its sidewalk seating and classic bistro fare make it one of the neighborhood's defining see-and-be-seen destinations.

name: Vernick Food & Drink
description: Chef Greg Vernick's James Beard Award-winning townhouse restaurant turns pristine seasonal ingredients into refined, ingredient-forward plates. The warm, understated dining room has long been considered one of Philadelphia's finest tables.

name: Friday Saturday Sunday
description: A revived 1970s institution, this intimate spot pairs inventive, Michelin-starred cooking with a beloved dining room that helped shape Philadelphia's modern restaurant scene. Its cream of mushroom soup has stayed on the menu for decades and is a genuine city classic.

name: My Loup
description: A stylish modern French restaurant just off the square from the team behind Vernick, serving elegant bistro plates in a lively, art-filled room. It quickly became one of the neighborhood's most talked-about openings and a go-to for a polished night out.

name: Her Place Supper Club
description: Chef Amanda Shulman runs this reservation-only supper club as a warm, communal dinner party with an ever-changing prix fixe. The cozy, home-kitchen atmosphere and hard-to-get seatings have made it one of Philly's most sought-after tables.

name: Wilder
description: Set inside a striking former dance academy, Wilder delivers elevated American cooking across multiple stylish levels near the square. Its wood-fired kitchen and handsome bar make it a versatile choice for both dinner and drinks.

name: The Love
description: A cheerful, farmhouse-chic restaurant from Aimee Olexy and Stephen Starr serving comforting seasonal American plates just steps from Rittenhouse Square. Its sunlit dining room and hearth-driven cooking make it a reliable favorite from brunch through dinner.

name: Oyster House
description: This longtime raw bar carries on a family seafood legacy with daily-shucked oysters, snapper soup, and a classic lobster roll. The bright, tiled dining room and happy-hour oyster deals keep it a dependable Center City staple.

name: Lacroix
description: The Rittenhouse Hotel's flagship restaurant overlooks the square and offers refined French-inspired fine dining in a serene, upscale setting. Its lavish Sunday brunch is a longstanding special-occasion tradition among Philadelphians.

name: Little Water
description: A contemporary coastal restaurant tucked on a quiet block near the square, focused on thoughtfully sourced fish and vegetable-forward plates. Its intimate room and creative crudo have earned it strong critical praise.

name: Dear Daphni
description: On the ground floor of The Laurel, this Michael Schulson restaurant offers a modern, shareable take on Mediterranean cooking built around mezze and grilled dishes. Its glamorous, buzzy dining room makes it a popular pick for group dinners near the square.
